task.description: Design lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md for REQ-025 (Event append). This is Letflow's first multi-table atomic transaction (Ecto.Multi across events/instance_sequence/instance_projections/idempotency-sidecar/event_payload_store) and first requirement needing tenant_id derived from the Ecto :prefix rather than accepted as a caller argument -- both need concrete, unambiguous design, not left to ELIXIR-DEV's judgment. Specify: the exact Ecto.Multi step order and each step's operation; the locking mechanism for instance_sequence (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE-equivalent in Ecto, exact query shape); the full StoreError-equivalent tagged-tuple/exception error set (one distinct, pattern-matchable case per named failure mode in the requirement text); how tenant_id is derived from :prefix by reversing schema_name_for_tenant/1 (name the reversing function and its signature); the metadata pre-transaction validation (>50 entries, key/value length limits, non-string values) and confirm it runs before the transaction opens, not inside it. Branch feature/WF02-REQ025-20260817 already exists and is checked out.
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md: design for Letflow.EventStore.append/2 (attrs, opts, opts requiring :prefix). Covers all 6 task items: (1) exact Ecto.Multi step sequence (M1 active-instance guard, M2 instance_sequence lock+increment via insert-if-absent + Ecto.Query lock:"FOR UPDATE" + update_all inc, M3 idempotency check/insert reusing TenantProvisioning's re-select-on-conflict idiom, M4 events insert, M5 conditional event_payload_store insert, M6 instance_projections upsert), with Registry validation (REQ-024's validate_payload/3) and metadata validation deliberately run BEFORE Repo.transaction opens (not as a Multi step), reasoned explicitly against invariants 8/9; (2) new Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (pure reverse of schema_name_for_tenant/1) plus a hard rule that append/2's attrs never accepts :tenant_id (rejected with :tenant_id_not_accepted rather than silently overridden, to satisfy AC6's 'must fail loudly' wording); (3) full tagged-tuple error set (append_error()) covering every named StoreError case; (4) metadata pre-transaction validation spelled out (>50 entries/key>128/value>1024/non-string, first-violation-wins); (5) full @spec for append/2 with :prefix-based tenant targeting. R-Co source (event_store.md/store.zig) reconfirmed absent on this host (find turned up nothing) -- worked from docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-025 text plus req023/024 design docs' own direct R-Co quotations, flagged explicitly in doc section 0 rather than presented as verified primary-source reading. Flagged one MAJOR open question (OQ-1): REQ-025's AC6 names instance_sequence and the idempotency sidecar as tables needing a correctly-derived tenant_id, but REQ-023's actually-shipped schema (verified directly against the .ex files and migration DDL) gives neither table a tenant_id column at all -- only events/instance_projections have one. Design states a concrete resolution (tenant isolation for those two enforced via :prefix schema boundary, not a column) and tells TEST-DESIGNER how to adapt AC6's test accordingly, rather than silently narrowing the acceptance criterion. Also flagged OQ-5 (MAJOR): instance_projections needs insert-if-absent (upsert), not a bare update, for a brand-new instance's first event, since nothing else in current scope creates that row -- read REQ-023's EE-01/S3 deferral as applying to engine-owned columns, not row creation, and asked REVIEWER to explicitly confirm this reading. No implementation code written -- signatures, type shapes, and prose/pseudocode algorithm steps only.
